question: Name the compound precipitated when the solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium iodide are mixed:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lead iodide.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lead iodide** is a **yellow precipitate** formed when the solutions of** lead(II) nitrate and potassium iodide** are mixed.
 
• Lead iodide is an** ionic compound** consisting of **lead cation (Pb2+) **and** iodide anion (I-).**
 
• It burns with a** green flame** and is a **good oxidizing agent.**
 
• It is extensively utilized in **seed clouds, printing, and photography.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Potassium oxide (K₂O)** is a** basic oxide** formed by the reaction of potassium with oxygen.

 
 
• It is a white solid with a **high melting point.**
 
 
 
• **Potassium sulphate (K₂SO₄)** is a salt that is commonly used as a** fertilizer**.
 
 
• It is formed by the reaction of** potassium hydroxide and sulfuric acid.**
 
 
 
• **Lead oxide (PbO)** is a basic oxide formed by the reaction of** lead with oxygen**.
 
 
• It is a yellow or red solid with a** high melting point.**
